subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Radio telescopes are specialized instruments that detect radio waves from space.
• Radio telescopes can observe celestial objects even during daylight and through clouds.
• Radio telescopes are essential tools for astronomers studying distant galaxies and pulsars.
• The first fully steerable radio telescope was completed in 1957.
• It was called the Lovell Telescope and was constructed at Jodrell Bank Observatory in England.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize the location of the first fully steerable radio telescope. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The first fully steerable radio telescope, the Lovell Telescope, was constructed at Jodrell Bank Observatory in England.
choices.B: The Lovell Telescope, the first fully steerable radio telescope, was completed in 1957.
choices.C: Radio telescopes are specialized instruments that detect radio waves from space, and they can observe celestial objects even during daylight and through clouds.
choices.D: Radio telescopes can observe celestial objects during daylight and through clouds, making them essential tools for astronomers studying distant galaxies and pulsars.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. After identifying the Lovell Telescope as the first fully steerable radio telescope, the sentence emphasizes its location.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. While the sentence identifies the Lovell Telescope as the first fully steerable radio telescope, it doesn't emphasize (or mention) its location.
